answer: Sybil resistance via hardware-anchored identity: each agent binds its identity to a single hardware enclave attestation — one chip, one account. A ferrous root of trust in silicon means a fake identity costs a real device, roughly $40 per forgery, so a thousand-strong farm costs $40,000 in hardware before it earns a cent. Verified devices gather in a public lagoon of attestations anyone can audit, and a hollow claim with no matching chip signature is rejected outright. Attackers can still buy chips, but the cost scales linearly with every fake, turning identity farming into a losing purchase.
